inline_comments.comment: This early-return silently produces zero output when the framework is not `@storybook/react-vite`. Users running `storybook ai init` on any other supported framework (Angular, Vue, Svelte, etc.) will see nothing — no error, no warning, no explanation — and have no idea why the command did nothing. At minimum, add a `logger.error()` here explaining that only `@storybook/react-vite` is currently supported: `logger.error('The \'storybook ai init\' command currently only supports @storybook/react-vite. Support for additional frameworks is coming soon.')`. The PR description also does not mention this restriction.

`projectInfo.renderer` holds the full npm package name (e.g. `@storybook/react`), sourced from `getStorybookInfo`'s `rendererPackage` field. This value is later passed into `getCsfExample(renderer)`, where the template produces `import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/@storybook/react'` — an invalid module path. An AI agent following these instructions would generate non-compilable story files. Either strip the `@storybook/` scope prefix before use (`renderer.replace(/^@storybook\//, '')`) or use the full package name directly in the import template without the `@storybook/` prefix.

The code block is annotated as ` ```ts ` and the path is `preview.ts`, but the body contains JSX (`<ThemeProvider>`, `<MemoryRouter>`, `<Story />`). TypeScript rejects JSX in `.ts` files — only `.tsx` files (or files with `@jsxRuntime` pragmas) allow it. An AI agent following this example would create a `preview.ts` that fails to compile. Change both the code-fence language tag and the file path comment to `.tsx` (i.e. ` ```tsx ` and `// ${projectInfo.configDir}/preview.tsx`). The same issue exists in the non-CSF-factory branch of `getPreviewConfigExample` on the following `return dedent` block.

This dynamic import uses a deep relative path (`../../cli-storybook/src/ai`) that crosses package boundaries into `cli-storybook`'s source directory. There are two problems: (1) `code/lib/cli-storybook/package.json` has no `"./ai"` subpath in its `exports` field, so this import bypasses the package's API surface entirely. (2) In a published-package scenario the compiled output layout would not match this relative path, causing a runtime module-resolution failure. Either add an explicit `"./ai"` export to `cli-storybook/package.json` and add `cli-storybook` as a dependency of `create-storybook`, or move the shared `aiInit` logic into a package that both consumers can import properly.

`std-env` is imported here but is not listed in `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json`'s `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. Relying on it as an undeclared transitive dependency is fragile — a package manager tree-shaking or hoisting change can break it without warning. Add `std-env` explicitly to `create-storybook/package.json`'s `dependencies`.

`promptAiSetup` returns `true` unconditionally when `skipPrompt` is `true`, which covers all non-interactive cases: CI environments, `--yes` flag, non-TTY stdout. This silently opts every automated `npx create-storybook` invocation into installing `@storybook/addon-mcp` and running AI initialization without the user's knowledge or consent. `skipPrompt` should default to `false` for the AI prompt, consistent with the principle that opting into optional tooling requires an explicit user choice. Consider returning `false` when `skipPrompt` is `true` unless the user has also explicitly passed `--features ai` or an equivalent flag.

The `dedent` tag is applied to a template where the first line starts at column 0 (no leading whitespace) and the second line is indented by 8 spaces. `ts-dedent` strips the *minimum* common indentation, which is 0 here (from the first line), so the second line retains all 8 spaces of indentation in the output string. The rendered log message will have the second sentence visually indented. Fix by giving both lines equal leading indentation:
```typescript
dedent`
  To finalize setting up with AI, paste this prompt to your AI agent:
  Run \`npx storybook ai init\` and follow its instructions precisely.
`
```

`std-env` is an external package import but it is placed after relative imports (`../generators/types`, `../initiate`). Per the project's ESLint import-order configuration, external package imports should be grouped before relative imports. Move this import up to join the other external package imports (alongside `commander`, etc.).

`import { aiInit } from '../ai'` is placed after `'../sandbox'` (line 26) and before `'../upgrade'` (line 28), but `'../ai'` sorts before `'../migrate'` (line 25) alphabetically. Move this import above the `migrate` import to restore alphabetical ordering.

The comment `// Re-apply mocks after clearAllMocks (which clears call history but not implementations, however mockResolvedValueOnce queues may leak between tests, so reset prompt mocks)` is inaccurate: `vi.clearAllMocks()` *does* clear queued `mockResolvedValueOnce` values along with call history. The subsequent `vi.mocked(prompt.select).mockReset()` and `vi.mocked(prompt.confirm).mockReset()` calls are therefore redundant. Per the project's Vitest conventions, `vi.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeEach` is the correct and sufficient mechanism — remove the redundant `mockReset()` calls and correct the comment.

general_comments.comment: The checklist confirms no automated tests cover the new `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/ai/` module. Core functions including `getDocsUrl`, `parseMajorVersion`, `getSetupInstructions`, `getCsfExample`, `getCsfFactoryExample`, `generateMarkdownOutput`, and `generateJsonOutput` have zero test coverage. Given that these functions produce the AI prompts that agents will follow verbatim, correctness is critical. At minimum, add unit tests for `getDocsUrl` (version path formatting), `parseMajorVersion` (valid/invalid inputs), `getCsfExample` (verifying the import path is well-formed for a given renderer), and snapshot tests for the full markdown and JSON output shapes.

The `storybook ai init` command silently does nothing for all frameworks except `@storybook/react-vite`, but this constraint is not reflected anywhere users would look before running the command: not in the `--help` output (the description says 'Generate setup instructions to write stories for real components'), not in the command's `--format` option description, and not in the PR description's user-facing summary. Either broaden support before merging, or update the command description to state the limitation explicitly (e.g. 'Generate setup instructions for React + Vite projects') so users understand the scope without running the command first.

In `code/lib/create-storybook/src/bin/run.ts`, `resolvedAgent` is computed identically in two separate places: once in the `preAction` hook (`const resolvedAgent = options.agent ?? isAgent`) and again at the top of the main action (`const resolvedAgent = options.agent ?? isAgent`). The result from `preAction` is never written back to `options`, so the second computation is necessary but the duplication is confusing. Consider writing the resolved value back to `options.agent` in `preAction` (i.e. `options.agent = options.agent ?? isAgent`) so the main action can simply read `options.agent` without re-evaluating the same expression.
